_doc: THE FRONT DOOR (docs/REINTERP_OPENING_DECISION_2026-07-24.md §2; the evolution of R28 §4 layer 1's orienting card, D43). ⚑ S162 / R3-01 + F-01 (his 2026-09-20): the panel wears the 1997 machine's own chrome — the ERA1 palette from src/desktop/theme/era1.ts, a title bar, bevelled buttons, an interim mark (the CRT, drawn in code; his logo file is still his ask and replaces it) — and it OFFERS THE CHOICES instead of listing them: three cards, one per way of being here (this computer · a phone or tablet · a headset), each with its own controls and its own entry button, and a checkbox for the sound captions. The phone card's button is the real gesture iOS demands before it grants orientation (CLAUDE.md, look-mode 3), so choosing it asks there and then; the headset card is pressable only when this browser has confirmed an immersive session. Frame voice, per CLAUDE.md's 'the frame never plays': functional, undecorated, no fiction — the chrome is the machine's, the words are the frame's. `premise` is the session brief's own wording (R9-canonized by Sérgio; verbatim). `contentNote` and `nameNote` are the ethics surfaces (ETHICS_CONSTRAINTS #4; 08_STATUS_REGISTER §8 decision 9) behind the 4 s arm-delay — kept whole. The captions choice is `ledger.view.captions` (in memory only, never stored): the sound NAMES in the strip (data/strings/captions.json, W-G2); spoken words and the piece's own lines always show.

subtitle: SurvivingSOGICE · University of Bergen, Center for Digital Narrative
premise: You will follow different lives through thirty years of one machine.
about: One computer, one room. The room ages around you and the software keeps updating. What the software is for is what you are here to see.
contentNote: This depicts how organised "conversion" networks target queer people online — in their own tactics and language. You can leave at any time; nothing you do is kept.
nameNote: One thing specifically, so it is not a surprise: in the last part, a system speaks a name that the person it is speaking to does not use. The piece is not neutral about this — the system is wrong. If you would rather not hear it said aloud, the menu (Esc, or the button in the corner) has a setting for that; the subtitles still show what the system did.
chooseNote: Choose one. You never walk, and nothing is timed — turning to look is the only thing your body has to do.

desktop.heading: On this computer
lines: Drag with the mouse to look around.
Click to choose, and to use things on the desk.
Click a marker on the floor to move to it.
Scroll to zoom the view in or out.

phone.heading: On a phone or tablet
lines: Turn the device to look around, as in a 360 video.
Tap to choose. A tap that slides is a look, not a choice.
Pinch to zoom in when something is too small to read.
phone.denied: Motion access was declined — you can still drag to look. Entering.

headset.heading: In a headset
lines: Turn your head to look around.
Point with the controller and pull the trigger to choose.
Squeeze the grip for the menu.
headset.unavailable: No headset found in this browser.

menuLine: Esc — or the corner button — opens the menu: pause, where you are, controls, credits, leave.
captionsLabel: Name every sound in the caption strip
captionsNote: Spoken words are always captioned. This adds the sounds — a modem, a chime, a room.
enterNote: The room is dark until you do.
